name: Gochang, Hwasun and Ganghwa Dolmen Sites
description: Across three areas of South Korea (Gochang and Hwasun in the southwest, and Ganghwa island near Seoul), more than a thousand dolmens stand in fields and on hillsides. These tombs of huge stone slabs, raised between roughly the 7th and 3rd centuries BC, marked the graves of the ruling elite. Korea holds about 40% of the world's dolmens, and few places show them so densely packed.
